title: Eastern Wei
capsule: Eastern Wei was one of the successor states of the Northern Wei dynasty, created in 534 when the strongman Gao Huan installed the puppet emperor Xiaojing Di at Yecheng after the court split with the western faction. Real authority lay entirely with Gao Huan and, after his death in 547, his son Gao Cheng and then Gao Yang. In 550 Gao Yang deposed Xiaojing Di, executed him the following year, and proclaimed the Northern Qi dynasty, bringing Eastern Wei to a formal close after only seventeen years of nominal existence. The state is significant as the vehicle through which the Gao clan consolidated military dominance over the North China Plain.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Eastern Wei's territory is well documented in Chinese dynastic histories; its borders with Western Wei were contested along the Wei River valley and are only approximately known.
